audit_findings.title: Gross cash add-back may double-count customer advances
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,775.139 million of contract liabilities plus $433.944 million of customer deposits, totaling $2,209.083 million; $1.65 per diluted share and 3.1% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash funded by customer advances while forecast OE may include profit from satisfying the associated contracts.
audit_findings.evidence: The contract liabilities represent (1) deferred product revenue related to the value of products that have been shipped and billed to customers and for which control has not been transferred to the customers, and (2) deferred service revenue, which is recorded when we receive consideration, or such consideration is unconditionally due, from a customer prior to transferring services to the customer under the terms of a contract.
audit_findings.explanation: The advances and gross cash add-back are demonstrated, but actual double-counting is not established because fulfillment costs, refunds, and the OE treatment are unreconciled. Even excluding the entire combined liability would reduce base value by at most about $1.65 per share, versus the $119.73 gap between the $52.53 base value and $172.26 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile contract liabilities and deposits to associated cash, fulfillment costs, refunds, and forecast working-capital unwind; rerun the bridge only if the identified adjustment exceeds the recorded advance balances or otherwise affects recurring OE.

audit_findings.title: Owner earnings may omit material working-capital reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 cash-flow-statement asset and liability changes consumed a computed $1,475.678 million; anchor OE exceeds operating cash flow less capital expenditures by $899.566 million, or 19.3% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Omitted normalized working-capital investment directly overstates the OE numerator and every explicit and terminal cash flow grown from it.
audit_findings.evidence: Our estimate of our significant purchase commitments primarily for material, services, supplies and asset purchases is approximately $ 5.97 billion as of June 30, 2026, a majority of which are due within the next 12 months.
audit_findings.explanation: The $4,666.7 million anchor closely resembles an earnings-plus-noncash-charges-less-capex construction, while FY2026 operating cash flow less $375.945 million of capital expenditures was only $3,767.134 million. Not every current-year balance-sheet movement is recurring, but a 19.3% anchor gap is large enough to materially alter scenario values and the buy-below price.
audit_findings.action: Build a multi-year operating working-capital schedule separating receivables, inventory, payables, contract liabilities, deposits, taxes, and nonoperating balances; normalize the investment required at each growth rate and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Existing uncertain-tax claims appear absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $275.3 million filed uncertain-tax-position payable obligation; approximately $0.21 per diluted share and 0.39% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any opening tax claim not already reflected in OE cash adjustments should reduce the cash bridge available to common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: We recorded unrecognized tax benefits of $257.8 million and $258.6 million for the years ended June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2025, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge shows no tax-claim deduction, although the filing reports $257.767 million of unrecognized tax benefits, $45.8 million of accrued interest and penalties, and a $275.3 million uncertain-tax-position payable obligation. The exact unprovided amount is unresolved, but deducting the full $275.3 million would reduce base value by only about $0.21 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $275.3 million obligation to current and noncurrent tax payables, accrued interest and penalties, and any OE cash adjustments; deduct only the resulting unprovided opening claim.

audit_findings.title: FY2026 OE may retain non-operating gains
audit_findings.magnitude: $58.8 million pretax identified gains, equal to 1.26% of anchor OE; a computed maximum base-value scale of about $826 million or $0.62 per share if all remained in OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring security, foreign-exchange, and tax-reserve gains would inflate the anchor OE and be compounded through explicit forecasts and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The change in Other expense (income), net during the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 compared to the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025 was primarily due to a net fair value gain of $28.0 million from an equity security, favorable foreign exchange fluctuation of $19.2 million, and release of a tax reserve of $11.6 million compared to the prior fiscal year, partially offset by lower interest income of $3.8 million.
audit_findings.explanation: Retention in the anchor is unresolved, but the filing identifies only $28.0 million of security gain, $19.2 million of favorable foreign exchange, and an $11.6 million reserve release. Applying the full pretax amount to the base operating-value-to-anchor multiple gives only about a 1.2% base-equity effect, insufficient to change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace all three gains through the FY2026 OE reconciliation, remove any after-tax amount still present, and confirm whether related foreign-exchange effects offset operating exposures.

audit_findings.title: Terminal OE may perpetuate an expiring tax advantage
audit_findings.magnitude: $120.9 million FY2026 tax-holiday benefit, equal to 2.59% of anchor OE and $0.09 of filed diluted EPS; immediate full-period capitalization at the base operating-value-to-anchor ratio would be about $1.70 billion or $1.27 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Failure to raise forecast tax expense after scheduled expirations would overstate later explicit-period OE and terminal OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The tax holidays were amended and renewed under substantially similar terms as of July 1, 2025, and are scheduled to expire through December 2032.
audit_findings.explanation: The expiration through December 2032 is demonstrated, but replacement tax rates and any forecast normalization are unresolved. The current annual benefit is only 2.59% of anchor OE; even the conservative scale of removing it throughout the entire base valuation is about 2.4% of base equity value, while the actual effect beginning after 2032 would be smaller under the same economics.
audit_findings.action: Map each holiday's expiration date and affected earnings, apply enacted post-expiration and Pillar Two rates, verify whether the anchor was already normalized, and rerun the later explicit years and terminal value.

audit_findings.title: Purchased-intangible amortization may be added back without replacement economics
audit_findings.magnitude: $190.8 million FY2026 amortization and $230.788 million total remaining scheduled amortization; recurring replacement economics are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding purchased-intangible amortization back to OE without charging normalized acquisition or replacement spending overstates sustainable OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Amortization expense for purchased intangible assets was $ 190.8 million, $ 220.4 million, and $ 239.3 million, for the fiscal years ended June 30, 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing quantifies amortization, but the record does not establish the D&A split used in OE or the spending required to replace acquired technology and customer relationships. Recent acquisition cash spending was zero in FY2025 and FY2026 and $3.682 million in FY2024, but that history does not establish the long-run acquisition requirement. The current amortization alone is about 4.1% of anchor OE; materiality of the economic replacement charge remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the full $190.8 million was added back, analyze a longer acquisition history and acquired-technology contribution, estimate normalized replacement spending, and rerun OE if an economic charge is supported.
